It consists of eight tuned, bossed metal plates strung on cord and set on a wooden antangan frame. In Maguindanaon the name means 'kulintang with strings', and it is also called kulintang a putao; the Maranao call it sarunay, the name more popular in North America. It is regarded as a relatively recent instrument, and many are made only from tin cans. In use it resembles the kulintang a kayo: it is played only for entertainment at home, and beginners learn new pieces on it before moving to the kulintang; in America, masters also use it to train students in large numbers.
